claim: Direct stochastic search on the step heights of f, starting from the constant profile and refining multiplicatively, beats the uniform seed substantially: it finds a non-uniform, edge-heavy profile whose autoconvolution is flatter than the triangle, raising R from 2/3 to ~0.82-0.83. The best results (p0002 at 0.833, p0006 at 0.822) come from coordinate/block-multiplicative hill climbing on the exa

Restricting f to a low-frequency cosine profile (edge-heavy, a>0) already lifts R to ~0.72 from 2/3, confirming that pushing mass toward the ends flattens f*f and raises the ratio, but the constrained family plateaus well below free-form search (~0.72 vs ~0.83), so the cosine parametrisation is too rigid to reach the optimum.

A two-level profile with a lower central region (central gap) raises R to ~0.70 from 2/3, so removing central mass does flatten f*f and help, but the gain is smaller than edge-heavy or free-form shapes (~0.70 vs ~0.72-0.83), indicating the central-gap mechanism is real but not the dominant route to the optimum.

The winning profiles share a signature: f*f's maximum sits off-centre (~0.40-0.50 of support) with a broad near-max plateau rather than a sharp central peak, and the profile is edge-heavy (largest/mean height ~2.3-2.7). Refining a good coarse shape at N=50 and then upsampling it and refining at successively finer N (150, 400) beats refining at a single resolution: starting from p0002's 0.833 N=50 shape, staged coordinate descent with block moves and smooth perturbations reached 0.850 at N=400, whereas earlier high-N searches that upsampled the constant seed stalled near 0.80-0.82. Jointly optimizing random nearby coordinate pairs on a small 2-D factor grid escapes the local optimum that single-coordinate accept-only moves get stuck in: on p0002's 0.833 N=50 shape, pairwise refinement reached 0.854 (largest/mean 2.92, f*f max at 0.47 of support), the best N=50 result so far, confirming that neighbour coupling matters and that the single-coordinate optimum was not tight.

Replacing ||f*f||_inf with a smooth L_p surrogate and optimizing all heights jointly by L-BFGS-B with analytic gradient gives only a small gain over coordinate descent: from p0002's 0.833 it reached 0.835 at N=50, well short of pairwise (0.854) or multi-resolution (0.850) refinement. Targeting the autoconvolution knots nearest the maximum — picking a knot with L[k] > 0.97*max and rescaling the two heights whose product forms it — beats blind pairwise moves: on p0009's 0.853861 N=50 shape it reached 0.857288 (+0.0034), the best N=50 result so far, and cut the fraction of knots within 0.1% of max from ~22% to 14.85%, confirming that the max knot is the binding constraint and tha

Pairwise moves still help at fine resolution but only marginally: applying p0009-style pairwise factor-grid moves inside p0011's upsample ladder on p0009's 0.853861 shape gave 0.854953 (+0.0011) at N=50, below the 0.857288 that max-targeted moves reached from the same start, so neighbour coupling is not the main lever once a good shape exists.

Whether 0.854-0.857 at N=50 is a local basin or near the true optimum is still open: a ~6% multiplicative basin-hop from the best, each trial run through a shortened pairwise refinement, recovered only +0.00003 (0.853891), and wide-loop variants adding gradient polishing (0.856709) or escalating resolution to 800 (0.854820) stayed below the max-targeted 0.857288 — consistent with a narrow basin bu

Running the max-targeted inner loop at each rung of an upsample ladder (N=50→150→400) lifts the N=50 max-targeted optimum: from p0017's 0.857288 at N=50, staged max-targeted refinement reached 0.857968 at N=400 (+0.00068). This is the first time max-targeted moves have been combined with a resolution ladder (p0019's blind-pair ladder stalled at 0.855), so fine resolution adds plateau flatness that

Prepending a smooth L_p continuation (large p→small) to the max-targeted hill climb gives a small but real gain: on p0017's 0.857288 N=50 shape it reached 0.857596 (+0.00031). The smooth stage reshapes the profile before discrete moves start, leaving f*f's max at 0.470 of support with 15.84% of knots within 0.1% of max. This is a larger gain than the pure smooth polish applied to the same start (p

Making max-targeted moves systematic (enumerating all valid splits of the top-3 near-max knots on a fine factor grid, plus Gaussian refinement) does not beat random targeting: on p0017's 0.857288 N=50 shape it gave only +0.000005 (0.857293). The random-split version already finds the useful reductions, so the bottleneck is the narrow N=50 basin (F10), not the choice of which split to try.

A pure smooth L_p polish (p=8,16,32,64) applied directly to p0017's 0.857288 N=50 shape barely moves it: +0.000004 (0.857292). The gradient step converges to essentially the same point, confirming that the N=50 max-targeted optimum is a genuine local basin that global gradient polishing alone cannot escape — the gain in p0020 comes from the smoother seed, not the polish.

Exact O(N) rank-2 incremental updates of the autoconvolution L (instead of a full np.convolve per candidate) make the max-targeted ladder affordable at fine resolution, and that extra iteration budget converts directly into score: on p0022's 0.857968 N=400 shape, the incremental evaluator with a 20-step inner refinement and an N=400→800 ladder reached 0.858188 (+0.00022) at N=800, the largest sing

Annealing a top-m mean surrogate (m from ~half the knots down to 1) to attack the near-max plateau, then polishing on exact R, does not move the score: on p0022's 0.857968 N=400 shape it returned exactly 0.857968 (-0.000000). The plateau of ~40% of knots within 5% of max is therefore not the binding obstruction — accepting surrogate-improving moves does not let the search cross to a better exact-R

Replacing the coarse 5x5 factor grid with a continuous single-height optimization (log-spaced factors plus golden-section refinement) on near-max knots gives no gain: on p0022's 0.857968 N=400 shape it ended at 0.857968 (-0.000000). The saturation is not caused by the grid resolution of the move primitive — a finer 1-D primitive on the same construction finds nothing the coarse grid missed.

Skipping the N=400 rung and pushing the fast incremental max-targeted ladder straight to N=1600 then N=2400 keeps paying: on p0031's 0.858188 N=800 shape it reached 0.858250 at N=2400 (+0.000062), the largest gain of the generation, with the f*f max at 0.450 of support and a broad near-max plateau (20% of knots within 0.1% of max). Low-frequency multiplicative basin hops (cosine/sign perturbations of the whole profile followed by a short fast relaxation slice, adopting only exact improvements) do move the N=800 optimum: on p0031's 0.858188 shape it reached 0.858222 (+0.000034), comparable to a resolution rung. This is the first basin move to succeed where the earlier slow-scored basin-hop (F10) failed, suggesting the earlier

An exact rank-1 fast evaluator with a full systematic sweep of every height (log-factor scan plus golden-section refine per coordinate) at N=800 returns the start unchanged: on p0031's 0.858188 shape it gave 0.858188 (-0.000000). Coordinate-wise the N=800 optimum is already a local max, so single-height moves — even exact and exhaustive — cannot improve it; only joint or global moves can.

Pushing the fast incremental max-targeted ladder to a finer rung keeps paying at the frontier: on p0034's 0.858250 N=2400 shape, a single N=4800 rung reached 0.858286 (+0.000036), and a separate run to N=5000 reached 0.858291 (+0.000040). The discretization of the continuous optimum is still not saturated at N=2400, so finer rungs convert iteration budget directly into score.

A contiguous Gaussian-bump block move (changing 10-80 neighbouring heights at once, evaluated exactly via two cheap convolutions) plus low-frequency perturbation polish on the N=2400 best gives a small real gain: on p0034's 0.858250 shape it reached 0.858265 (+0.000014).
